structures.name: Urinary Bladder
structures.function: Stores urine (up to 500 ml); detrusor muscle contracts during micturition; trigone between ureteric orifices and internal urethral orifice
structures.location: Extraperitoneal, in the space of Retzius; retroperitoneal when empty, rises into abdomen when full; posterior to symphysis pubis
structures.bloodSupply: Superior vesical artery (from umbilical artery), inferior vesical artery (male), vaginal artery (female), from internal iliac artery
structures.innervation: Parasympathetic (detrusor contraction): S2-S4 via pelvic splanchnic nerves. Sympathetic (internal sphincter): T10-L2. Somatic (external sphincter): S2-S4 via pudendal nerve
structures.clinicalNotes: Bladder cancer: transitional cell carcinoma most common; painless haematuria. Cystocele: descent of bladder into vagina. Neurogenic bladder in spinal cord injury. Suprapubic catheter if urethral catheterisation impossible.

structures.name: Sigmoid Colon
structures.function: Stores and propels faeces; absorbs water; peristaltic contractions move content to rectum
structures.location: S-shaped loop; from left iliac fossa into pelvis to the level of S3 where it becomes the rectum; has a mesentery (sigmoid mesocolon) allowing mobility
structures.bloodSupply: Sigmoid arteries from inferior mesenteric artery
structures.innervation: Parasympathetic: pelvic splanchnic nerves S2-S4. Sympathetic: lumbar splanchnic via inferior mesenteric plexus
structures.clinicalNotes: Sigmoid volvulus: commonest site of colonic volvulus; large gas-filled loop on AXR. Diverticulosis commonest in sigmoid colon. Sigmoid colectomy for diverticular disease or carcinoma. Left ureter crosses iliac vessels at pelvic brim — at risk in sigmoid resection.

structures.name: Rectum
structures.function: Stores faeces until defecation; has three lateral folds (valves of Houston) and the rectal ampulla; peritoneum covers upper 1/3 anteriorly and laterally, middle 1/3 anteriorly only, lower 1/3 extraperitoneal
structures.location: Begins at S3 (junction with sigmoid), follows sacral curve, ends at anorectal junction (puborectalis sling level); 12-15 cm long
structures.bloodSupply: Superior rectal artery (from IMA), middle rectal (from internal iliac), inferior rectal (from pudendal)
structures.innervation: Parasympathetic: S2-S4 pelvic splanchnic. Sympathetic: hypogastric plexus. Pain below dentate line: somatic (pudendal nerve)
structures.clinicalNotes: Total mesorectal excision (TME): sharp dissection in the mesorectal fascial plane is key to curative rectal cancer surgery. Anterior resection for upper rectal cancer; abdominoperineal resection (Miles) for very low rectal cancer. Nervi erigentes (S2-4) at risk → impotence post-rectal surgery.

structures.name: Internal Iliac Artery
structures.function: Main blood supply to pelvic organs, gluteal region, and medial thigh; divides into anterior and posterior divisions
structures.location: Arises from common iliac artery at the pelvic brim (L5-S1); descends medially into the pelvis; anterior division supplies pelvic viscera, posterior division supplies gluteal and posterior thigh muscles
structures.clinicalNotes: Internal iliac ligation: used to control pelvic haemorrhage (PPH). Uterine artery embolisation for fibroids. Obturator artery anastomoses with inferior epigastric → 'corona mortis' — bleeds if divided inadvertently in hernia repair.

structures.name: Obturator Nerve
structures.function: Motor to medial compartment thigh adductors; sensory to medial thigh; passes through obturator canal
structures.location: Arises from lumbar plexus L2-L4; descends medial to psoas major; exits pelvis through obturator canal; divides into anterior and posterior branches supplying medial thigh
structures.clinicalNotes: Obturator hernia: uncommon; compressed nerve causes pain radiating to medial thigh (Howship-Romberg sign). At risk in pelvic lymph node dissection and paravaginal repair. Obturator nerve block for hip adductor spasm.

structures.name: Pudendal Nerve
structures.function: Main sensory and motor nerve of the perineum; supplies external anal and urethral sphincters, external genitalia, and perineal skin
structures.location: Arises from sacral plexus S2-S4; exits pelvis through greater sciatic foramen; wraps around ischial spine; re-enters pelvis via lesser sciatic foramen into pudendal canal (Alcock's canal) in obturator internus fascia
structures.clinicalNotes: Pudendal nerve block at ischial spine for perineal pain or delivery analgesia. Pudendal neuralgia: chronic perineal pain, worse sitting, improved standing. Stretch injury during prolonged labour causes stress incontinence. Ischial spine landmark for sacrospinous fixation.

structures.name: Uterus
structures.function: Site of implantation and fetal development; body (corpus), cervix, and fundus; endometrium undergoes cyclical changes; myometrium contracts in labour
structures.location: Anteverted and anteflexed in nulliparous women; between bladder anteriorly and rectum posteriorly; supported by broad ligament, uterosacral ligaments, round ligament, and cardinal (Mackenrodt's) ligament
structures.bloodSupply: Uterine artery (from internal iliac); ovarian artery (from aorta at L2)
structures.innervation: Parasympathetic: S2-S4. Sympathetic: T10-L1 (pain of labour referred to T10-L1 dermatome)
structures.clinicalNotes: Uterine artery crosses over the ureter 2 cm lateral to cervix ('water under the bridge'). Must identify ureter during hysterectomy to avoid ligation. Uterine fibroids: commonest benign tumour in women. Ectopic pregnancy: most common in ampulla of fallopian tube.

structures.name: Prostate Gland
structures.function: Produces seminal fluid (citrate, zinc, PSA, acid phosphatase); surrounds proximal urethra; divided into peripheral, central, and transitional zones
structures.location: Below the bladder neck, above the urogenital diaphragm; anterior to rectum (palpable on PR examination); encircles prostatic urethra
structures.bloodSupply: Inferior vesical artery and middle rectal artery (from internal iliac)
structures.innervation: Parasympathetic: pelvic splanchnic S2-S4. Sympathetic: hypogastric plexus T10-L2
structures.clinicalNotes: BPH: transitional zone enlargement causing lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS). Prostate carcinoma: peripheral zone; raised PSA; treated with radical prostatectomy, radiotherapy or hormone therapy. Neurovascular bundles posterolaterally must be preserved to maintain potency in nerve-sparing prostatectomy.

structures.name: Sacral Plexus
structures.function: Provides motor and sensory innervation to lower limb, perineum, and pelvis; lies on piriformis muscle
structures.location: Formed from lumbosacral trunk (L4-L5) and ventral rami S1-S3 on the anterior surface of piriformis, converges to form the sciatic nerve which exits through the greater sciatic foramen
structures.bloodSupply: Vasa nervorum from lateral sacral and inferior gluteal arteries
structures.clinicalNotes: Piriformis syndrome: piriformis muscle compresses sciatic nerve causing sciatica-like symptoms. Pelvic fracture may injure sacral plexus. Pre-sacral neurectomy: division of superior hypogastric plexus for chronic pelvic pain.

structures.name: Levator Ani
structures.function: Pelvic floor support; maintains anorectal angle with puborectalis; involved in micturition, defecation, and continence; supports pelvic organs
structures.location: Three parts: pubococcygeus (pubis to coccyx), puborectalis (sling around anorectal junction), iliococcygeus (ilium to coccyx); forms the pelvic diaphragm
structures.bloodSupply: Inferior gluteal artery, inferior vesical, and pudendal arteries
structures.innervation: Inferior rectal nerve (S2-S4) and direct branches from S3-S4
structures.clinicalNotes: Levator ani avulsion during childbirth → pelvic organ prolapse. Levator ani syndrome: chronic anorectal pain. Repair during perineal reconstruction post-abdominoperineal resection. Key structure in total pelvic floor repair.
